reading.body:
CyrusOne OCB1 Council Bluffs in Council Bluffs, Iowa, publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 120,000 square feet of technical space, operated by CyrusOne.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 900 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 225 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

CyrusOne OCB1 Council Bluffs holds 6 published certifications: PCI DSS (the standard required to handle payment card data), HIPAA (handling of protected health information), FISMA (a specific compliance or security standard), HITRUST (a healthcare-focused security framework built on top of HIPAA), SSAE 18 (the attestation standard underlying SOC reports), TIA-942 (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

Iowa has 2 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 2 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 18 MW. CyrusOne OCB1 Council Bluffs contributes 9 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
